Alphabet is seeking up to US$25 billion from latest bond sale
article:
(Aug 6): Alphabet Inc is looking to raise as much as US$25 billion from its latest US investment-grade bond offering, a deal that will test investor appetite for AI-related debt following a July selloff.

No final decision has been made on the size, according to people familiar with the matter, asking not to be identified as they’re not authorized to speak publicly.

The Google and YouTube parent is offering notes in as many as 10 parts, with maturities ranging from two to 40 years, a separate person said. Initial price talk for the longest-tenored tranche is a premium of about 1.55 percentage points above Treasuries.

Bank of America Corp, Citigroup Inc, Goldman Sachs Group Inc, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo & Co are managing the sale, the person added. BofA and JPMorgan declined to comment while Alphabet and the other banks didn’t immediately respond.

Alphabet’s offering comes two weeks after the company’s raised 2026 spending outlook helped trigger fresh worries about whether massive artificial-intelligence investments will pay off. Investor appetite for bonds to help fund those expenditures cooled in July as Alphabet increased its forecast to as much as US$205 billion, more than double 2025’s outlays.

A BlackRock Inc-linked firm last week sold US$12.5 billion of bonds tied to a Meta Platforms Inc data center project in Texas. Initial demand was lackluster, following soft interest for an offering by Amazon.com Inc. Newly issued AI-related notes from firms including SpaceX saw spreads widen in the secondary market.

See also: AI’s volatile power demand is damaging its own data centres

But the environment improved as August began, helped by gains in US Treasuries.

“We’ve had a few days now of positive reactions from investors across corporates and especially technology,” said Brett Kozlowski, portfolio manager at GW&K Investment Management. “But another large debt deal will still test the depth of that and be worth watching.”

Alphabet, which sold more than US$50 billion of debt in the first half of 2026, and Amazon have led the AI-infrastructure borrowing spree. Alphabet last tapped the US high-grade debt market in February, before selling bonds in Swiss francs, British pounds, euros, Canadian dollars and Japanese yen. It also issued nearly US$85 billion of shares two months ago.

See also: Nintendo tops estimates with tariff refunds and Switch 2 games

Capital spending contributed to Alphabet posting its first quarter of negative cash flow since its 2004 initial public offering.

title: China books 13 more US soy cargoes, nearing quarter of target — Bloomberg
article:
(Aug 6): China booked another flurry of US soybean cargoes, as the country makes headway towards fulfilling the purchase pledge made as part of a trade truce struck last year.

The country’s state-owned firms bought at least another 13 soybean cargoes — or roughly 800,000 tonnes — on Wednesday, according to people familiar with the matter. That comes on top of 488,000 tonnes announced by the US Department of Agriculture on Monday, which marked the biggest daily sale for China this year, and another 132,000 tonnes announced on Tuesday.

It brings the country’s total purchases for the 2026-27 season to about six million tonnes, said the people, asking not to be named as they were not authorised to talk to the media.

That would be close to a quarter of the way towards meeting the at least 25 million tonnes of US soybeans the White House has said China will buy annually through 2028. The target was announced as part of the trade truce struck by President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping during their late October summit in South Korea.

The two leaders met again in Beijing in May, after which the US announced that China will also buy at least US$17 billion of US agricultural products annually over the same period, on top of the soybean pledge. The amount will be prorated for 2026, the White House said.

The shipments are mainly for loading from September and will come from both the US Gulf and Pacific Northwest, the people said. The purchases come after a recent decline in prices, with Chicago soybean futures trading near a one-month low.

See also: US defence agency cancels plan to buy US$300 mil of lithium

Still, even as agricultural purchases continue, US-China tensions have been rising again as both sides escalate technology and trade restrictions. Bloomberg has also reported that there are US concerns over China’s compliance with the trade deal, highlighting the fragility of the current détente.

Beijing recently stiffened drone export controls and sanctioned US entities. That move came after the Federal Communications Commission’s ban on some foreign-made robots and power inverters and the blacklisting of more than 40 Chinese companies accused of using forced labour.

Still, a spokesperson for China’s Commerce Ministry signaled Beijing’s willingness to keep relations on track. Trump has previously said that he expects to meet again with Xi in late September.

See also: Copper marches closer to US$14,000 as flows to US tighten market

title: Yangzijiang Maritime sells four newbuild bulk carriers
article:
Maritime financial solutions provider Yangzijiang (YZJ) Maritime Development has signed contracts to sell four newbuild bulk carriers of approximately 40,000 deadweight-tonne each, with vessel deliveries slated between April 2027 and May 2028.

The firm also updated that it had on July 30 delivered the first of four new medium-range tankers which were sold for an aggregate US$180 million announced in November 2025. The second tanker is expected to be delivered in November and the remaining two in 2027.

In total, YZJ Maritime has entered into sale contracts to monetise a total of 12 newbuild vessels for an aggregate gross value of US$500 million over a nine-month period.

“Our ability to consistently originate, invest, monetise, and recycle maritime assets is central to the Group's long-term growth strategy and a core differentiator of Yangzijiang Maritime,” says YZJ Maritime executive chairman and CEO Ren Yuanlin. “The continuous sale of our newbuilds demonstrates the repeatability of this business model, allowing us to crystallise value at attractive points in the market cycle, reinvest capital into the next pipeline of opportunities.”

Shares in YZJ Maritime remained flat at 60 cents on Aug 6.

title: China launches cybersecurity review into Palo Alto Networks
article:
(Aug 6): China launched a formal security review of products sold in the country by US technology firm Palo Alto Networks Inc, ramping up pressure on the company months after accusing it of harbouring links to intelligence services.

The Cyberspace Administration of China said in a statement on Thursday that the review was necessary to protect critical infrastructure, citing a pair of national security laws. Shares in Palo Alto Networks fell as much as 4.2% before later paring losses in pre-market trading.

Beijing accused a host of American and Israeli firms including Palo Alto Networks earlier this year of being connected to spy agencies, though it didn’t provide evidence of those claims. At the time, a government directive seen by Bloomberg News, which also named Fortinet Inc and Check Point Software Technologies Ltd, said that Chinese companies’ use of US and Israeli cybersecurity products could result in sensitive data being sent overseas.

The government told Chinese organisations to identify whether they use any cybersecurity products from the designated companies and to replace any of those with domestic technologies by the first half of 2026.

Palo Alto Networks didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The company has multiple offices in China, including locations in Beijing, Shenzhen, Shanghai and Guangzhou, according to its website.

Its threat intelligence arm, Unit 42, has published a body of research on Chinese hacking operations, including a report last year that accused them of breaching email servers of foreign ministers as part of a years-long effort targeting the communications of diplomats around the world.

See also: China’s services gauge hits two-year low as firms turn cautious

title: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding announces record RMB5.37 billion net profit for 1HFY2026
article:
Mainboard-listed Yangzijiang (YZJ) Shipbuilding has reported a 28.4% y-o-y rise in net profit to a record RMB5.37 ($1.02) billion for 1HFY2026 ended June 30. No dividend was declared.

Revenue surged 36.2% y-o-y to RMB 17.5 billion, which was attributed to the progressive construction of vessels secured at higher contract prices, a favourable product mix, and the commencement of shipbuilding activities at the Hongyuan Yard.

Gross profit grew 42.8% y-o-y to a record RMB6.35 billion, while gross margin expanded 170 basis points to 36.2%, mainly driven by the progressive construction of vessels secured at higher contract prices. Net profit margin declined to 30.6% from 1HFY2025’s 32.5%.

On a segmental basis, revenue from shipbuilding jumped 34.8% y-o-y to RMB16.5 billion; shipping revenue rose 14.5% y-o-y to RMB585 million; and others (including terminal services, trading, manufacture and sale of steel pipe products, ship design services and investment property) increased 270% y-o-y to around RMB436 million.

During the first-half of the year, the company secured US$1.75 ($2.24) billion new orders for 38 vessels, which included 25 containerships, 10 oil tankers, two gas carriers and one bulk carrier. As at June 30, orderbook stood at US$22.4 billion across 256 vessels, with deliveries scheduled through to 2030. In July, the shipyard secured additional US$0.21 billion new orders for 4 oil tankers, bringing total new orders secured in 2026 to approximately US$1.96 billion as at end-July.

YZJ Shipbuilding executive chairman and CEO Ren Letian says that the company's record revenue and profitability reflects the company’s “prudent” cost management and “sophisticated” shipbuilding capabilities.

See also: Newly listed JustCo posts US$0.8 mil net loss for 1HFY2026

He adds: “Order-win momentum remains healthy as we secured US$1.96 billion in new orders for the first 7 months of the year, with our 2029 delivery slots nearly full. Having delivered 27 vessels out of our 58-vessel target for 2026, we remain committed to the timely delivery of high-quality, sophisticated vessels and the realisation of our orderbook, creating long-term value for all stakeholders.”

Shares in YZJ Shipbuilding closed at $3.94 on Aug 6, down two cents or 0.5% from the previous close.

title: Credit Bureau Asia reports 2% y-o-y increase in patmi to $5.5 million for 1HFY2026, declares 2.2 cents dividend
article:
Credit and risk information solutions provider Credit Bureau Asia (CBA) has reported a 2% y-o-y rise in patmi to $5.5 million for 1HFY2026 ended June 30. Basic and diluted earnings per share rose to 2.4 cents and the company declared an interim dividend of 2.2 cents, which is 10% higher y-o-y.

Revenue grew 2.7% y-o-y to $31 million while net profit before income tax (NPBT) increased by 3.9% to nearly $16 million, according to the company’s bourse filing on Aug 6.

On a segmental basis, revenue and NPBT for its financial institution (FI) data business grew 4% in 1HFY2026. The company says that Credit Bureau Singapore continues to maintain its growth trend, while Credit Bureau Cambodia continues its recovery momentum from 2025, and operational performance from Myanmar Credit Bureau continues to improve.

Meanwhile, revenue and NPBT for CBA’s non-FI data business grew 1% and 3% respectively in 1HFY2026. The non-FI data business is continuing its growth momentum from 2HFY2025 as businesses around the world adjust to the changing global trade policy shifts, according to the announcement.

CBA says that it remains “cautiously optimistic” on growth for the remaining 2026 financial year, in light of an uncertain global business environment.

Shares in the company closed at $1.08 on Aug 6, down one cent or 1%.

title: SGX reports 'standout' FY2026; bumper dividend brings full-year payout to 57 cents
article:
For the year ended June 30, SGX reported $759.5 million in adjusted net profit attributable to equity holders of the company, up 24.6% y-o-y, a record. Operating revenue less transaction-based expenses in the same period was up 13.9% to $1.48 billion, also a record.

To reward shareholders, SGX plans to pay a final quarterly dividend of 11.5 cents, up from 10.5 cents in the year-earlier. In addition, SGX plans to pay a one-off additional dividend of 12.5 cents. This will bring total payout for FY2026 to 57 cents – again another record - up from 37.5 cents paid for FY2025.

SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye calls FY2026 another "standout year" for the company he has helmed since 2015. "Growth was broad-based, with our cash equities business leading the way and our foreign exchange and commodities pillars reaching new volume highs. This reflects the resilience of our multi-asset strategy and the progress we are making across the group."

The various segments did well but unsurprisingly, the equities business was the standout, accounting for 34% of SGX's total net revenue, up from 30.3% in FY2025. From $392.7 million in FY2025, this amount jumped to $502.9 million.

In particular, SGX's revenue from trading and clearing was up 36.3% to $302.3 million, on the back of a 34.9% jump in securities daily average value $1.8 billion. In FY2026, total securities traded value increased 35.5% to $455.7 billion.

Loh says SGX is entering the current FY2027 from "a position of strength". SGX will extend its franchise through strategic index partnerships and new ecosystems such as gold; unlock more value by bringing its listed and over the-counter FX capabilities closer together; and use data more effectively to deepen client relationships and identify opportunities across the exchange’s businesses.

See also: Venture Corporation reports 5.6% y-o-y rise in earnings for 1HFY2026, raises interim dividend to 30 cents

"Gains from capital recycling enable us to reward shareholders this year with a proposed one-off additional dividend, reflecting our disciplined approach to capital management," says Loh.

The IPO scene - constant under scrutiny - saw a pick up after a dismal FY2025, with just six listings. In FY2026, there were a total of 21 new listings that raised a total of $4.1 billion - nowhere near the likes of Hong Kong but a marked difference versus just $25.7 million raised in FY2025. Secondary fund raisings were lower, however, with $3.6 billion, down from $4.3 billion.

SGX says it is "well-positioned" to deliver its medium-term guidance of 6-8% growth in revenue, and low- to mid-single digit expense increase. This current FY2027, SGX expects continued broad-based growth across all operating segments. SGX expects 6-8% increase in expenses and capital expenditure of around $100 million.

"Active and disciplined capital management remains a key priority, balancing strategic investments and capital recycling with sustainable shareholder returns. We remain confident in delivering the planned quarterly dividend increases of 0.25 Singapore cents through FY2028," says SGX.
